page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / Tom's tantrum
title: Tom's tantrum
topic: Language to persuade someone to change their mind
description:
There's confusion at the offices of Tip Top Trading. Anna has announced that 'yes' she will accept Mr Socrates's offer of a promotion but Tom thinks she is accepting his marriage proposal. How will he react when the penny drops - or in other words, when he finds what she really means?
This episode focuses on the language that you might use to get someone to change their mind.
phrases: Don't rush into making a decision.

listening_challenge.question: What word does Tom use to say he is leaving the company?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Welcome back to the offices of Tip Top Trading where there's a bit of confusion. Anna…

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: I think Tom's got the wrong end of the stick.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: But I didn't give him a stick.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: No, no. I think there's been a misunderstanding. When you said your answer was 'yes' he thought you meant 'yes, I'll marry you'!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh no! I meant yes to the promotion. Gosh I've got to sort this out. Tom, Tom, hold on please.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: We can't hang about Anna. Let's fix a date, invite everyone – even Paul.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: No, no, we can't.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: You're right, not Paul – he just talks about biscuits.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: No. I mean 'no', we can't get married. I meant yes to the promotion. I can't marry you.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: What? So when you said 'yes' you meant 'no'?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: I see. Right, that's it. Anna, I've made it very clear what I think about you and you… you… just throw it back in my face. I've had enough… enough of you… enough of this company. I quit!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Anna. I think he's upset. He's having a tantrum.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: A tantrum – is that serious?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Not really. Maybe you need to calm him down and make him change his mind. Tell him 'not to be too hasty', 'don't rush into a decision' and say 'we can work this out' – you can can't you?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I think I can. Tom, please, don't be too hasty. Let's talk about this. We can work something out, just don't rush into making a decision – please. You're my best – my only – sales executive.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Sorry Anna – I'm a free spirit. I must go where the wind takes me. You've had your chance, now it’s mine. I’m off.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Wow, I've never seen Tom be such a… man. Will this be the last time we ever see him?
Here are some of the phrases Anna used to try and get Tom not to leave:
Don't be too hasty
Don't rush into making a decision
We can work this out

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: …erm, sorry, I just forgot to take my special mug. Bye.
